specs.anchorText: in which almost nothing changes between consecutive samples. That redundancy is the opportunity.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a cheerful little robot stands at the end of a fast-moving conveyor belt of film frames, each frame a near-identical photo of a walking dog that has nudged slightly to the right. The robot, wearing a tiny detective hat, points a magnifying glass at two adjacent frames and draws a small green motion arrow between them, looking calm and pleased. A wall clock above ticks at thirty, hinting at thirty frames per second, but no readable text. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. The humor is gentle: the robot keeps up effortlessly with an endless parade of barely-changed pictures. specs.alt: A detective robot at the end of a conveyor belt of nearly identical film frames of a walking dog, using a magnifying glass to draw a small motion arrow between two consecutive frames, illustrating that video is a dense stream of barely-changed images whose tiny frame-to-frame differences are what motion estimation reads.
specs.caption: Video is not a pile of unrelated photographs; it is the same picture, nudged thirty times a second, and motion is the story we tell about the nudge.

specs.anchorText: viewed through a small window (and a derivative is the smallest window there is), a moving edge only reveals its motion across itself
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a puzzled cartoon character peers through a short cardboard tube held to one eye, looking at a long diagonal striped pole sliding past. Through the small round opening of the tube, only a single diagonal edge is visible, and the character confidently points a red arrow straight across the edge, while behind them, unseen, the pole is actually sliding sideways shown by a faint gray arrow. A small thought bubble shows just the tiny circular view with one edge. The style should be friendly and approachable, like a comic strip or an XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive and warm, clean white background, generous margins. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle humor: the character is sure of a motion direction that is only half the truth. Keep the composition focused on one clear metaphor: looking through a tiny aperture, you can only see motion across an edge, never along it.
specs.alt: A character looking through a small cardboard tube at a sliding striped pole, seeing only one diagonal edge through the opening and confidently pointing an arrow across the edge while the pole is really sliding sideways, illustrating the aperture problem where local data reveals only the motion component perpendicular to an edge.
specs.caption: Through a small enough window, a moving edge will only ever confess the part of its motion that crosses the window; the sideways slide stays a secret.

specs.anchorText: the matrix that Lucas-Kanade must invert to compute flow is the matrix whose eigenvalues Harris and Shi-Tomasi threshold to declare a corner
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a friendly robot inspector walks along a checkerboard wall holding a small clipboard, giving a cheerful green thumbs-up and a gold star to a sharp checkerboard corner, a hesitant shrug at a plain straight edge, and a confused frown at a totally blank flat patch. Above each spot, small simple icons hint at the verdict: a happy double-arrow cross at the corner, a single arrow at the edge, nothing at the blank patch. The same corner also wears a tiny badge as if it were a recognized landmark, suggesting it is both findable and followable. The style should be friendly and approachable, like a comic strip or an XKCD-inspired infographic, warm and expressive, clean white background, generous margins. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle humor in the robot's escalating confusion from corner to blank wall. Keep the composition focused on one clear metaphor: corners are trustworthy to track, edges only partly, blank regions not at all.
specs.alt: A robot inspector grading three spots on a checkerboard wall: a gold star and cross-arrows for a sharp corner, a shrug and single arrow for a plain edge, and a frown for a blank flat patch, illustrating that the same well-conditioned structure tensor makes corners both matchable and trackable while edges and flat regions are underdetermined.
specs.caption: The points worth detecting are exactly the points worth following: a corner has enough information to pin its motion in both directions, an edge in only one, and a blank wall in none.

specs.anchorText: It makes the pixel adopt the average opinion of its four neighbors, who adopted theirs
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a grid of round pixel characters laid out like neighbors over a fence. At one corner, a single pixel near a textured moving square holds up a clear green arrow pointing right; the news travels hop by hop across the grid as each neighbor leans toward the next and whispers, passing along a copy of the arrow that grows slightly fainter and blurrier with each retelling, until distant blank pixels in the corner finally hold up a pale, fuzzy version of the same arrow. The chain of leaning, whispering pixels is the focus. The style should be friendly and approachable, like a comic strip or an XKCD-inspired infographic, warm and expressive, clean white background, generous margins. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle humor: a motion estimate in a blank region is literally a rumor passed down a line of gossiping pixels. Keep the composition focused on one clear metaphor: smoothness fills silent regions by diffusing a neighbor's flow outward, getting blurrier with distance.
specs.alt: A grid of cartoon pixel characters passing a rightward motion arrow hand to hand from a textured moving square out into blank regions, the arrow growing fainter and blurrier with each hop, illustrating how Horn-Schunck's smoothness term diffuses flow from textured pixels into flat ones that carry no data of their own.
specs.caption: A flow vector in the middle of a blank wall is a rumor that travelled hundreds of pixel-to-pixel hops from the nearest edge, getting blurrier with every retelling.

specs.anchorText: keep reporting a crisp, confident bounding box around the wrong thing, frame after frame, with the serene certainty
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a small earnest tracker robot proudly holds a bright green bounding-box frame around a drifting gray cloud (or a floating balloon), beaming with total confidence, while the actual target it was supposed to follow, a red ball, rolls away in the opposite direction completely ignored. A faint dotted trail behind the robot shows how it slowly slid off the ball and onto the cloud over several steps. The robot's expression is cheerfully, obliviously certain. The style should be friendly and approachable, like a comic strip or an XKCD-inspired infographic, warm and expressive, clean white background, generous margins. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle humor: the tracker is supremely confident about the wrong object and has no idea. Keep the composition focused on one clear metaphor: appearance trackers drift and then keep reporting a confident box around the wrong thing.
specs.alt: An earnest tracker robot beaming with confidence as it holds a green bounding box around a drifting cloud while the red ball it was meant to follow rolls away ignored, with a dotted trail showing the slow drift, illustrating how an appearance tracker latches onto the wrong object and keeps reporting a confident box without realizing it has failed.
specs.caption: A drifting tracker never sounds unsure; it follows the wrong exit with the serene certainty that the highway will come back, which is exactly why you must check its confidence flag, not just its box.

specs.anchorText: The Hungarian algorithm solves that assignment optimally, and SORT
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a cozy little control-room scene staffed by friendly robots running a multi-object tracker as an assembly line. On the left, a forecasting robot looks at a crystal-ball-style screen predicting where several numbered, colored dots will appear next (the Kalman predict step). In the middle, a matchmaker robot stands at a board drawing the best one-to-one lines connecting predicted positions to a fresh batch of incoming detection markers (the Hungarian assignment). On the right, two clerk robots manage a small filing cabinet, one stamping a brand-new ID badge onto an unmatched newcomer (birth) and one gently retiring a folder that has gone unclaimed too long (death). Numbered ID tags on the tracked dots stay consistent across the stations. The style should be friendly and approachable, like a comic strip or an XKCD-inspired infographic, warm and expressive, clean white background, generous margins, uncluttered. Suitable for a technical textbook. Minimal labels: a few short numbers on the ID badges are acceptable, otherwise no text or lettering. Keep the composition focused on one clear metaphor: multi-object tracking is a small dispatch room that predicts, matches, updates, and manages births and deaths of identities every frame.
specs.alt: A control-room of friendly robots running multi-object tracking as an assembly line: a forecasting robot predicting where numbered dots will appear, a matchmaker robot drawing optimal one-to-one lines between predictions and incoming detections, and clerk robots issuing new ID badges and retiring stale ones, illustrating the SORT pipeline of Kalman prediction, Hungarian assignment, and track birth and death.
specs.caption: A multi-object tracker is a tiny dispatch office: predict where everyone will be, optimally match each new sighting to an existing identity, then issue badges to newcomers and retire the ones who stopped showing up.
